, for the total inclusive cross section, the theoretical uncertainties are dominated by the scale dependence.
NNLO effects in heavy-quark-annihilation Higgs production are moderate and well understood.
the total Higgs production cross section in heavy-quark fusion processes is known to NNLO in QCD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the NNLO corrections for the total inclusive cross section of charged and neutral HIGGS production in heavy-quarks annihilation are rather small, of the order of 5%, and that they can be well described by a simple rescaling with the corresponding parton luminosites.

, in the context of the $$b\overline{b}\phi$$bb¯ϕ production channel, the inclusion of NNLO QCD corrections is sufficient to reduce the theoretical uncertainties in the cross section to a level comparable to that of the experimental uncertainties, and that the inclusion of the full NNLO partonic cross section in the calculation of the Higgs signal at the LHC will have only a small impact on the final result.
, for the total inclusive cross section, the NNLO corrections to the $$b$$b and $$t$$t processes are about 20% and 10% respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NNLO QCD corrections to heavy-quark annihiliation processes can be computed with very little effort.
the partonic cross sections for the $$b\overline{b}\phi$$b¯bϕ, $$c\overline{c}\phi$$c¯cϕ and $$t\overline{t}\phi$$t¯tϕ processes are identical.
the total inclusive cross section is very well approximated by a rescaled LO result, and that NNLO corrections are small and can be safely neglected for all initial-state quark pairs.
